licence.name: driver's licence (private and light goods vehicles)

note: Read 2026-10-30 on the Land Transport Authority's own site (lta.gov.ws). Its Samoa National Road Code (version 0.1, edited 22 September 2020): a person over 16 can apply for a learner's permit (valid 3 months, not held); a person who has reached 17 can apply for a driver's licence for a private and light goods vehicle, issued after the theory and practical tests on payment of the fee, and its table of age limits gives 17 for a car, so the full licence is held from 17 (the age the held file lacked, which had held the learner's 16). The LTA's page on drivers licences: a new drivers licence, valid for 5 years, costs $173 for local citizens and $315 for overseas citizens (the page adds "to sit theory and practical"), held as the citizen's fee and a non-citizen's (foreignFee); the same page breaks the local fee down as $35 a year ($173), but the fee is held as the five-year licence's, not by the year. The learner's permit ($79), the commercial classes and the temporary licence for visitors aren't held. The identity card is not this office's; no exchange list was read. The page's WST 315 for 'overseas Citizens (to sit theory and practical)' is the fee to sit the tests, not the licence's, so it isn't held as a non-citizen's licence fee (the lead, 2026-10-30).
